frozen_candidate_root_contribution: An agent's binding fixing of a determinate future: to undertake that a specified future point will come to pass, such that it stands either to be realized/made-true or to be defaulted-on. The fixed point may be an outcome delivered to a party (reward or threat) or a time/place of encounter; that variation is objectal, not nuclear. Valence (benefit vs. harm), truth-value (kept vs. broken), whether the committer is the causer/enactor, and mutuality are all EXTERNAL to the root -- supplied by context, by other roots (Sdq/Hqq/xlf), or by the III/VI augment.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: An agent's binding fixing of a determinate future: to undertake that a specified future point will come to pass, such that it stands either to be realized/made-true or to be defaulted-on. The fixed point may be an outcome delivered to a party (reward or threat) or a time/place of encounter; that variation is objectal, not nuclear. Valence (benefit vs. harm), truth-value (kept vs. broken), whether the committer is the causer/enactor, and mutuality are all EXTERNAL to the root -- supplied by context, by other roots (Sdq/Hqq/xlf), or by the III/VI augment.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root w-`-d marks a bindable undertaking about a fixed future -- a commitment that some future thing (a deliverable held out to someone, or an appointed time/place to meet) will happen. It is deliberately morally neutral: the very same verb yaEidu is used by Satan promising poverty and by God promising forgiveness in one verse (2:268). It is also not self-guaranteeing: whether the undertaking is kept is asserted separately with other words (Hqq 'comes true', Sdq 'proves truthful', xlf 'defaults'), which is why God is repeatedly said to 'not default on the mii`aad' (39:20) while Satan admits 'I promised you, then I betrayed you' (14:22). Because it is bindable, it differs from a mere prediction or plain speech.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: wEd does NOT entail: (1) a good/favourable outcome -- it freely takes the threat pole (Satan promises poverty 2:268; God promises Hell to the hypocrites 9:68; the entire wa`iid set 14:14/50:14-45; Form IV threatening 7:86); (2) truth or fulfilment -- Satan's wa`d is broken (14:22) and mere delusion (4:120,17:64), fulfilment being asserted only from OUTSIDE via Hqq/Sdq/'laa yuxlifu'; (3) mutuality -- Form I is one-directional (giver to recipient); reciprocity is added only by Forms III/VI; (4) a neutral chronological point -- unlike ajal/waqt/miiqaat, wEd's appointed time (maw`id/mii`aad) is always someone's COMMITTED point, subject to xilaaf (note 7:142 reserves miiqaat, w-q-t, for the resulting term while keeping waa`adnaa for the act of appointing); (5) covenant relationship -- it is distinct from `ahd (contrasted directly in 20:86), being the announced deliverable rather than the standing covenant; (6) mere report/prediction -- the 'wa`dan `alayhi Haqqan / mas'uulan' and 'laa yuxlifu' framing marks it as a claim-generating commissive.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 20:58-59 and 8:42 are purely neutral human scheduling (the magicians' appointed place/day and Badr's mutual battle-rendezvous) with no benefactor, no reward/threat content and no divine actor, which disproves any narrow 'promise of an outcome' nucleus; yet 20:58 itself frames that meeting as maw`idan laa nukhlifuhu ('an appointment neither of us will default on'), re-importing the identical khilaf/binding semantics of the divine-promise cases, so it lowers the claim altitude to a broad 'binding fixing of a determinate future' rather than fracturing the root.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: Two related-but-distinct, functionally-separated senses: (A) {waEada, waEd, waEiid, awEada IV, mawEuud, passives} = 'undertake to bring about a future outcome (reward/threat) for someone'; (B) {mawEid, miiEaad, waaEada III, tawaaEada VI} = 'fix/agree a time-or-place of encounter'. Its best support is a real distributional gap: the base noun waEd is NEVER a neutral meeting, and the neutral-meeting sense NEVER uses waEd (only the m-nouns / Forms III-VI); plus the Form III duration cluster (2:51/7:142 'thirty/forty nights', 20:80 'the side of the mount') where the object is a bare time-span/place with God as sole actor. This competitor is DEFEATED, not by lexicon but Quran-internally, by three demonstrated bridges: (a) 9:114 'maw`idatin wa`adahaa iyyaahu' -- an m-noun used for a pure promise and glossed by the Form I verb in the same clause; (b) 20:80 (Form III verb) <-> 20:86-87 (mawEid noun) <-> 'axlaftum maw`idii' all naming one event; (c) the xilaaf/Hqq predicate pair operates identically on both poles -- 'laa nuxlifuhu' (neutral meeting, 20:58) ~ 'laa yuxlifu ...l-mii`aad' (divine promise, 39:20); 'faHaqqa wa`iid' (threat, 50:14) ~ 'wa`da ...llaahi Haqq' (promise, 10:55). Because the classes co-instantiate in single words (mawEid = appointed place OF Fire/Hell/the Hour: 11:17, 15:43, 54:46), they are not disjoint.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge that the naive 'promise = good outcome' sense is internally DISPROVEN (2:268 minimal pair; 9:68; the wa`iid set) and that valence, truth, causation and mutuality are external to the root. They further converge that a single nucleus holds ACROSS all six form-classes, but only at a broad altitude ('binding fixing of a determinate future, outcome or encounter, realizable or defaultable'). The bridge between the outcome-branch and the appointment-branch is genuinely demonstrated Quran-internally (9:114 m-noun as pure promise; 20:80<->20:86-87 one event across Form III verb and mawEid noun; mawEid as appointed place of Fire/Hell/Hour welding appointment and threat; mii`aad as the very waEd God 'does not default on'), and the shared xilaaf/Hqq/Sdq predicate frames are the strongest single evidence that all forms name ONE binding-future relation rather than homonyms. The result is rated MODERATE, not STRONG: the surviving nucleus is broad, and the appointment branch (Form III duration cluster 2:51/7:142; bare-place 20:80; neutral tryst 2:235) genuinely sheds the 'outcome-held-out-to-a-recipient' payload, so identity of sense across the branches is defensible but not decisive; the non-vacuity of the broad nucleus rests specifically on the recurrent default/realization predicate frames, without which it would risk fitting everything.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form I active and passive verb -- the unilateral commissive core: an agent binds a specified future outcome to a recipient (X undertakes future Y to Z), valence- and truth-neutral. Active: yaEidu/waEada/naEidu/taEidu/imperative Eid; passive yuwEadu/tuwEadu/wuEida = 'that which is held out to you' (reward or doom that arrives).
clusters.classification_rationale: Polarity is contextual not root-borne, proven in a single verse (2:268 Satan yaEidu poverty // God yaEidu forgiveness). Reward pole 24:55:1, 21:103:11; threat pole 9:68:1, 22:72:24, 36:63:5, 46:17 (threatened resurrection), the 'fa'tinaa bimaa taEidunaa' challenge-formula. Bindability (not mere speech) shown by 'wa`dan `alayhi Haqqan/mas'uulan' and the 'laa yuxlifu' frame; broken by Satan (14:22:11).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 70 occurrences (qac_pos=V with no derived verb-form). Valence-neutral minimal pair 2:268; truth-external (14:22:11 broken; 39:74/30:6 kept from outside); causer-external (46:17, 23:35 resurrection the speaker cannot enact).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Verbal noun waEd -- the committed thing itself; content-neutral (needs an adjective for polarity: 'wa`dan Hasanan' 20:86). Bears the recurrent realization predicates (Haqq 10:4/10:55/30:6/31:9, maf`uulan 17:5/17:108, ma'tiyyan 19:61, Sadaqa 36:52, ghayru makdhuub 11:65) and the claim-generating frame ('`alayhi Haqqan' 9:111, 'mas'uulan' 25:16).
clusters.classification_rationale: waEd names the deliverable/entitlement, distinct from `ahd (covenant), directly contrasted in 20:86 ('yaEidkum ... wa`dan Hasanan' vs 'al-`ahd'). Scoffers' 'mataa haadhaa l-wa`d' (21:38, 34:29, 67:25, 73:18) shows the base noun states no fixed term -- the term lives in mawEid/miiEaad.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 49 occurrences. Same-verse contrast of God's true wa`d vs Satan's broken wa`d (14:22:8/9 vs 14:22:11).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: FiEiiL noun waEiid -- the threat-pole lexicalization of the same held-out-future: every occurrence is punitive/eschatological (khaafa wa`iid 14:14; yawm al-wa`iid 50:20; faHaqqa wa`iid 50:14).
clusters.classification_rationale: Not a separate root-sense but the negative reading the Form I verb already carries (10:46, 7:70/77, 46:17), morphologically frozen to the threat pole. Bridges to the promise pole via the SAME Hqq predicate: 'faHaqqa wa`iid' (50:14) ~ 'wa`da ...llaahi Haqq' (10:55).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form IV (tuwEidu, 7:86) -- morphologically fixed to the adversarial threat pole: 'you threaten/lie in wait and bar from the way of God'.
clusters.classification_rationale: Same threat reading the Form I verb already carries, here binyan-fixed; consistent with the wa`iid specialization.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Passive participle mawEuud (85:2, 'al-yawmi l-maw`uud') -- 'the appointed/held-out Day': the future point fixed as bound to come, valence supplied contextually (eschatological).
clusters.classification_rationale: Participial nominalization of the core relation; the Day is the fixed future that will arrive, bridging outcome and appointed-time senses.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: maf`il noun mawEid -- the appointed juncture (place, time, or occasion) of the committed future. Hinge cases weld appointment and threat: appointed PLACE of Fire/Hell/the Hour (11:17 'fal-naaru maw`iduhu', 15:43, 54:46); appointed time of doom (18:58/18:59); neutral human rendezvous (20:58-59); divinely-fixed deadline (18:59).
clusters.classification_rationale: Bridges the branches within single words: 20:80 (Form III verb) <-> 20:86-87 mawEid <-> 'axlaftum maw`idii' name one event; mawEid = appointed place OF the eschatological outcome, so appointment and outcome co-instantiate. Object thins toward the fixed juncture but keeps the binding/default semantics (20:58 'laa nuxlifuhu').
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 12 occurrences. Bridge/hinge nouns 11:17, 15:43, 54:46; 20:86-87 tie mawEid to the Form III verb and to xilaaf.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Feminine maf`il noun mawEidah (9:114) -- a PURE promise: Ibrahim's undertaking to his father, glossed in-clause by the Form I verb ('`an maw`idatin wa`adahaa iyyaahu').
clusters.classification_rationale: Decisive bridge: an m-prefixed noun (the morphology of the appointment branch) used for a plain promise and explicitly defined by the Form I verb -- so the m-nouns and waEd are not sealed lexemes; the m-prefix is not a hard wall between the two senses.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 1 occurrence (9:114), the single most direct bridge between the appointment-noun morphology and the promise sense.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: mifEaal noun miiEaad -- the committed appointed term/rendezvous. Both poles in one noun: the divine promise God 'does not default on' (3:9, 3:194, 13:31, 39:20 'laa yuxlifu l-mii`aad') and the battle-rendezvous parties disagree over (8:42); the appointed Day (34:30).
clusters.classification_rationale: miiEaad IS the waEd named from the term-angle: 'laa yuxlifu l-mii`aad' applies the same xilaaf predicate as 'laa yuxlifu ...llaahu wa`dah' (30:6), welding appointment and promise. Bridges the two branches.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 6 occurrences. The 'laa yuxlifu l-mii`aad' formula (3:9/3:194/13:31/39:20) is the strongest lexical bridge from the appointment-noun to the kept-promise sense.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Forms III (waaEada) and VI (tawaaEada) -- reciprocal/mutual fixing of an appointed tryst (time or place). 20:80 'the side of the mount' (place); 2:51/7:142 'forty/thirty nights' (time-span); 2:235 clandestine marriage pact; 8:42 mutual battle-rendezvous.
clusters.classification_rationale: Mutuality is contributed by the III/VI augment, not the bare root. The object here is a time/place juncture, the thinnest 'outcome' reading -- but stays bridged: 20:80 (III) is renamed by 20:86-87 mawEid + xilaaf, and 8:42 (VI) sits beside the miiEaad of the same event. Base Form I lacks this mutuality.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 5 occurrences (4x III: 20:80, 2:235, 2:51, 7:142; 1x VI: 8:42). This is where the appointment sense is most exposed.

reconciliation.rationale: The clause itself glosses it with the Form I verb ('maw`idatin wa`adahaa iyyaahu') and it denotes a pure promise, proving the m-noun morphology and the waEd sense are not sealed lexemes -- it is the decisive bridge, so it supports rather than resists the unified nucleus.

The same event is renamed by 20:86-87 with the mawEid noun and the xilaaf predicate ('axlaftum maw`idii'), tying the Form III verb, the appointment noun, and the default frame into one binding-future relation -- the bridge holds.

adversarial_verification.notes: The adversarial attempt tried to fracture the root into two unbridged senses (outcome-delivery vs scheduling) using its strongest evidence -- the distributional gap plus the Form III duration cluster (2:51/7:142/20:80) and neutral rendezvous (20:58-59/8:42/2:235). The refutation was defeated Quran-internally by three demonstrated bridges (9:114 m-noun as pure promise glossed by the Form I verb; 20:80<->20:86-87 one event across Form III verb, mawEid noun, and xilaaf; mawEid = appointed place of Fire/Hell/Hour and mii`aad = the waEd God 'does not default on'), so no occurrence fails the broad nucleus. Falsifiability is demonstrated because the NARROWER scopes ('promise of reward' / 'commit to deliver an outcome') made risky predictions that WERE falsified by 20:58-59/8:42/2:51/7:142, forcing the claim down to the broad altitude. Distinctiveness holds via the xilaaf (default) and Hqq/Sdq (realization) predicate frames that mark wEd as a bindable commissive -- distinguishing it from mere prediction/qawl, from `ahd (covenant, contrasted at 20:86), and from neutral chronology ajal/waqt/miiqaat (7:142 reserving miiqaat for the term).

independent_verification: Cross-checked against all three lenses: A and B independently affirm the demonstrated bridges and the valence/truth/causation externalities; the adversary C concluded a unified nucleus holds at the broad altitude with bridges demonstrated and no genuinely resistant occurrence. The residual reservation (broad nucleus flirts with over-generality, and the appointment branch thins the outcome payload) is recorded and is why result_strength is MODERATE rather than STRONG.
candidate_root_contribution: An agent's binding fixing of a determinate future: to undertake that a specified future point will come to pass, such that it stands either to be realized/made-true or to be defaulted-on. The fixed point may be an outcome delivered to a party (reward or threat) or a time/place of encounter; that variation is objectal, not nuclear. Valence (benefit vs. harm), truth-value (kept vs. broken), whether the committer is the causer/enactor, and mutuality are all EXTERNAL to the root -- supplied by context, by other roots (Sdq/Hqq/xlf), or by the III/VI augment.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 151 confirmed occurrences (Tanzil verse_text + QAC morphology): 70 Form I verbs, 49 waEd, 12 mawEid, 6 waEiid, 6 miiEaad, 4 Form III, 1 mawEidah, 1 Form IV, 1 Form VI, 1 ADJ mawEuud. Anchored by same-verse pairs 2:268 and 14:22.
layer_attribution.derivation: Base Form I supplies unilateral commitment; the III/VI augment adds reciprocity/mutual appointment; the maf`il/mifEaal nouns (mawEid, miiEaad) denote the appointed juncture; FiEiiL (waEiid) and Form IV freeze the threat pole; the passive participle (mawEuud) nominalizes the fixed future point. Morphology tracks branching without fracturing the nucleus.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: waEiid is a lexicalized threat-noun; mawEid/miiEaad are lexicalized appointment/term nouns. These specializations are Quran-internally bridged to the base commissive, not sealed off (9:114 m-noun = plain promise).
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Valence (reward vs. threat), the identity of the committer (God, Satan, humans, parents), and the specific content (forgiveness, poverty, Hell, resurrection, a meeting place) are contributed by context, NOT by the root; e.g. 2:268 fixes polarity by object alone.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary RESISTANT readings of 9:114 and 20:80 (apparent appointment-branch severance) were reconciled to CONSISTENT by in-text bridges (Form I gloss at 9:114; mawEid+xilaaf renaming at 20:86-87); appointment/rendezvous cases were held inside the broad nucleus via the shared default/realization predicate frames.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: No occurrence finally resists the broad nucleus; residual tension is that the surviving nucleus is broad and the appointment branch (2:51/7:142/20:80/2:235/8:42) sheds the richer 'outcome-to-a-recipient' payload, making whole-root identity of sense defensible but not decisive (hence MODERATE, and the recorded ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY/STRUCTURAL_ATYPICALITY hard cases).

hard_cases.reason: Neutral human scheduling with no benefactor/reward/threat/divine actor disproves a narrow 'promise of an outcome' nucleus; retained only because 'laa nuxlifuhu' re-imports the binding/default semantics, forcing the claim down to the broad altitude.

evidence_basis.statement: The magicians' neutral human appointment, but framed as 'maw`idan laa nuxlifuhu naHnu wa-laa anta' -- re-importing the identical khilaf/binding semantics of the divine-promise cases, which is why this neutral scheduling case still names a binding-future relation rather than mere chronology.

hard_cases.reason: Mutual battle-rendezvous with no promiser/promisee asymmetry and no valence defeats 'assurance to a recipient', surviving only under the broad 'fixed future juncture' nucleus.

evidence_basis.statement: Form VI mutual battle-rendezvous ('law tawaa`adtum la-ixtalaftum fi l-mii`aad'): no benefactor, no reward/threat content, no promiser/promisee asymmetry -- pure coordination of a meeting-point, defeating any 'assurance of an outcome to someone' reading and surviving only under the broad 'commit to a fixed future juncture' nucleus.

hard_cases.reason: Form III with a bare time-span object and God as sole actor is the thinnest 'outcome' reading; the Quran uses a different root (miiqaat, w-q-t) for the resulting term, exposing the appointment sense.

evidence_basis.statement: Form III with a bare time-span object ('forty nights') and God as sole actor: the 'outcome-held-out-to-a-recipient' schema is at its thinnest and the verse reaches for a DIFFERENT root, miiqaat (w-q-t, 7:142 'fatamma miiqaatu rabbihi'), to name the resulting term while reserving waa`adnaa for the act of appointing -- it resists the committed-outcome-delivery reading but not the broad nucleus, since the same Musa narrative supplies 'axlaftum maw`idii'/'maa axlafnaa maw`idak' (20:86-87) keeping it inside 'binding appointed future'.

hard_cases.reason: Parallel Form III duration case, thinnest outcome reading, term named with miiqaat not wEd.

evidence_basis.statement: Parallel to 2:51 ('thirty nights'): bare time-span object, God sole actor, and the resulting term named with miiqaat (w-q-t) not wEd -- thinnest outcome reading, held inside the broad nucleus by the mawEid/xilaaf framing of the same episode (20:86-87).

hard_cases.reason: Most bleached, symmetric, purely human use (secret marriage tryst) where the 'declared outcome accruing to a party' is barely visible.

evidence_basis.statement: Form III clandestine marriage tryst ('laa tuwaa`iduuhunna sirran'): mutual, purely human, no divine giver, no reward/threat, no term named -- the most bleached and symmetric use, where the nucleus's 'declared outcome accruing to a party' is barely visible; survives only under the appointment-branch reading of Forms III/VI.

hard_cases.reason: Divinely-fixed deadline for destruction with no recipient assured, resisting the recipient-directed assurance element.

evidence_basis.statement: 'wa-ja`alnaa li-mahlikihim maw`idan' -- a divinely-fixed DEADLINE for destruction: no one is 'assured' anything, resisting the recipient-directed assurance element, but held inside the broad nucleus as a binding appointed future point.

hard_case_representation.rationale: No occurrence is finally RESISTANT to the claimed broad nucleus: the appointment/rendezvous cases resist only the narrower 'outcome-to-a-recipient' reading, and each is held inside the nucleus by a demonstrated Quran-internal bridge (xilaaf framing at 20:58; mawEid+xilaaf renaming of the Form III event at 20:86-87; the m-noun-as-promise at 9:114). They are therefore recorded as adversarial boundaries and structural atypicalities, each with an evidence_basis statement persisted verbatim in the matching occurrence_override note or strongest_counterexample.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: The claim that a single universal nucleus ('binding fixing of a determinate future, outcome or encounter, realizable or defaultable') holds root-wide would be rejected if the appointment branch (Forms III/VI + mawEid/miiEaad) were shown to have NO Quran-internal bridge to the outcome branch -- i.e., if the neutral-rendezvous cases carried no binding/default semantics and no single word or episode co-instantiated both the appointment and the promise senses.
rejection_condition.search_location: The hinge/bridge occurrences 9:114 (mawEidah glossed by waEada), 20:80 vs 20:86-87 (Form III verb renamed by mawEid + xilaaf), 11:17/15:43/54:46 (mawEid = appointed place OF Fire/Hell/Hour), and the 'laa yuxlifu l-mii`aad' formula (3:9/3:194/13:31/39:20) vs 'laa yuxlifu ...wa`dah' (30:6).
rejection_condition.verification_method: Check whether the xilaaf (default) and Hqq/Sdq (realization) predicate frames attach to BOTH branches, and whether any single occurrence uses appointment morphology for a plain promise or appointment-noun for a kept promise; if none do, the branches are disjoint and the universal claim fails.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Distinguish genuine root-internal bridging from mere morphological relatedness or translation-gloss coincidence: require the bridge to be an actual co-instantiation in Quranic text (e.g., 9:114's in-clause verb, 20:86-87's cross-form renaming), not an inherited lexical assumption; exclude the term-noun miiqaat (w-q-t) which the text keeps separate.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If the branches prove unbridged, downgrade to claim_scope=LOCAL / claim_scope_kind=UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY (two-class result: outcome-delivery vs appointment/rendezvous) with research_state=UNRESOLVED, abandoning the universal nucleus.

reopen_conditions: Reopen if the Form III duration/place cluster (2:51, 7:142, 20:80) or the mutual-rendezvous cases (8:42, 2:235) are shown to carry NO xilaaf/Hqq binding semantics, severing the appointment branch from the outcome branch and forcing a two-class (UNRESOLVED) result.

Reopen if the bridge occurrences are re-analysed such that 9:114 (mawEidah), 20:86-87 (mawEid renaming the 20:80 Form III event), or the 'laa yuxlifu l-mii`aad' formula (39:20/13:31/3:9/3:194) no longer co-instantiate appointment and promise -- i.e., if the m-noun/miiEaad forms turn out disjoint from waEd.

Reopen if any occurrence of the base noun waEd or a Form I verb is found functioning as a purely neutral meeting/rendezvous (no held-out outcome, no benefactor), which would collapse the distributional gap the unified account relies on.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The adversarial attempt tried to fracture the root into two unbridged senses (outcome-delivery vs scheduling) using its strongest evidence -- the distributional gap plus the Form III duration cluster (2:51/7:142/20:80) and neutral rendezvous (20:58-59/8:42/2:235). The refutation was defeated Quran-internally by three demonstrated bridges (9:114 m-noun as pure promise glossed by the Form I verb; 20:80<->20:86-87 one event across Form III verb, mawEid noun, and xilaaf; mawEid = appointed place of Fire/Hell/Hour and mii`aad = the waEd God 'does not default on'), so no occurrence fails the broad nucleus. Falsifiability is demonstrated because the NARROWER scopes ('promise of reward' / 'commit to deliver an outcome') made risky predictions that WERE falsified by 20:58-59/8:42/2:51/7:142, forcing the claim down to the broad altitude. Distinctiveness holds via the xilaaf (default) and Hqq/Sdq (realization) predicate frames that mark wEd as a bindable commissive -- distinguishing it from mere prediction/qawl, from `ahd (covenant, contrasted at 20:86), and from neutral chronology ajal/waqt/miiqaat (7:142 reserving miiqaat for the term).
